Heterozygous carrier of the rs117385980 minor T allele. In two independent and small cohorts the T allele was less frequent among the oldest and longest-lived participants than among younger or earlier-deceased ones, which is a possible negative association with exceptional lifespan. Both results fell short of conventional significance (p = 0.074 and p = 0.073), the Finnish study reported 28% statistical power, and neither cohort had mortality follow-up. Treat this as a preliminary signal and not as a lifespan prediction.
negatives: Opposing observation in the same 2025 cohort: the T allele was absent from the frail group (0 of 39) and present in 8 of 188 non-frail participants, so it tracked with robustness even as it thinned out with age. That comparison was not significant (p = 0.36) and the adjusted odds ratio for frailty was 0.96. The authors raise antagonistic pleiotropy as one possible reading of the two directions together.

conclusion: Homozygous for the rs117385980 minor T allele. Neither of the two studies behind this module observed a single homozygote — 8 heterozygotes in 227 Iranian subjects and 12 in 198 Finnish men, and no T/T in either — so nothing here supports a conclusion for this genotype in either direction. The genotype does occur: gnomAD records 183 homozygotes in 574,784 alleles. Both studies analysed alleles rather than homozygotes, and extrapolating a doubled effect from their allele counts would be an inference they do not make. Deliberately unweighted and undirected: this row exists to say the question was not answered, not to leave a carrier unannotated.
